05-062.r: Manufacturing sector includes large, small scale, micro and medium industries; construction industry is not part of the manufacturing sector.

05-063.r: MSME revised definition: announced in Atmanirbhar Bharat Package 13th May 2020; notified 1st June 2020; effective 1st July 2020; one composite formula for manufacturing and service units.
05-063.t: Don't confuse notification date (1st June 2020) with the date it came into effect (1st July 2020).
hi: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (सूक्ष्म, लघु एवं मध्यम उद्यम)

05-065.r: 1991 Policy: SSI limit Rs. 60 lakh (was 35), ancillary Rs. 75 lakh (was 45); MSMED Act 2006; micro now: investment ≤ Rs. 1 crore, turnover ≤ Rs. 5 crore.

05-070.r: MSMED Act 2006, old manufacturing limits (plant and machinery): micro up to Rs. 25 lakh; small Rs. 25 lakh to 5 crore; medium Rs. 5 to 10 crore.
05-070.t: These are the old 2006 limits; the revised definition uses a composite investment-plus-turnover formula.

05-074.r: Medium enterprise (w.e.f. 1st July 2020): investment up to Rs. 50 crore, turnover up to Rs. 250 crore (not Rs. 15-25 crore); all MSME bank loans are priority sector.

05-075.r: Most registered factories → Tamil Nadu (ASI 2021-22: 39667), then Gujarat, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh.

05-076.r: SSIs get preference and reservation because they give higher employment per unit of capital and promote regional dispersion of industries.

05-077.r: Small scale and cottage industries are encouraged in India mainly because they generate large employment opportunities.

05-078.r: Small scale and cottage industries are important because they provide more employment.

05-079.r: Most important small scale industry of India → Handloom (unorganised sector); fourth Handloom Census 2019-20: about 35.23 lakh workers.

05-080.r: Largest industry of Uttar Pradesh by employment → Handloom (not cotton mills, leather or cement).

05-081.r: SSI problems: lack of capital, marketing experience and raw material; also old technology, power shortage, labour problems and industrial sickness.

05-082.r: Strikes and lockouts are a problem of large scale industries, not SSIs; SSIs face finance (working capital), marketing and raw material problems.

05-083.r: SSI committees in order: Karve 1955 → Nayak 1991 → Abid Hussain 1995 → S.S. Kohli 2000 (order IV, I, II, III).
05-083.c: Correct order IV, I, II, III is in no option; book says UPPSC key's option (c) is wrong.

05-084.r: Nayak Committee (RBI, 9 December 1991, P.R. Nayak) → finance problems of small scale industries; report September 1992.
05-084.t: Don't confuse with P.J. Nayak Committee (RBI, January 2014) on governance of bank boards.

05-085.r: Abid Hussain Committee (Expert Committee on Small Enterprises, 1995) → total abolition of reservation of items for small scale industries; report 1997.

05-087.r: Small scale sector's share in manufacturing gross turnover (since 1992) → about 40%; MSME share in manufacturing GVA 40.83% in 2021-22.

05-088.r: Cotton textile → high growth in cooperative units (14.8% yearly growth, 1999-2000 to 2005-06).

05-089.r: Textile industry → largest employer after agriculture: about 45 million direct and 60 million indirect jobs.

05-091.r: Largest quantity of cotton textile in India is produced by the powerloom sector (not mill, handloom or hosiery).

05-092.r: Largest textile centre in India (among Ahmedabad, Kanpur, Mumbai, Surat) → Mumbai.

05-093.r: Most cotton textile mills → Tamil Nadu (then Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh); Tamil Nadu has almost half of India's cotton spinning capacity.
05-093.t: Most mills = Tamil Nadu; most mill-made cotton cloth = Gujarat.

05-094.r: Highest mill-made cotton cloth production → Gujarat (2016-17), then Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh.

05-095.r: Oldest large scale industry of India → cotton textiles; first cotton mill set up in 1818 at Fort Gloster near Kolkata.

05-096.r: First industry to develop in India → cottage industry (since ancient times; declined under British rule).

05-097.r: Iron and steel → most basic industry of modern civilisation; backbone of the modern industrial economy.

05-098.r: Nepanagar (Burhanpur, Madhya Pradesh) → newsprint paper; Nepa Mills pioneered newsprint in India, production from April 1956.

05-099.r: Paper industry centres: Yamunanagar (Haryana), Guwahati (Assam), Ballarpur (Maharashtra); Shahabad is not known for paper.

05-100.r: Hazira (Surat, Gujarat) KRIBHCO fertilizer complex → based on natural gas.

05-101.r: India not self-reliant in fertilizers: urea above 85%, phosphatic above 50% self-sufficient, potash fully imported; India is second in nitrogenous fertilizers; fertilizer is second industry after iron and steel.
05-101.t: At question time only (c) was wrong; by present data (b) 'third largest in nitrogen' is also wrong (India is second).

05-102.r: Unused natural gas → best used for fertilizers; natural gas is main feedstock for ammonia (Haber process).

05-103.r: ONGC → set up 14 August 1956 as a Commission; statutory body October 1959; became Corporation in 1994.
05-103.t: Don't confuse 1956 (set up) with 1959 (statutory body by Act).

05-104.r: Oil India Limited (OIL) → exploration, development and production of crude oil and natural gas (not import or marketing).

05-105.r: MMTC → largest non-oil importer; PEC Ltd (STC subsidiary, 1971) → Ministry of Commerce & Industry; enforcing quality control is not an ECGC objective.

05-106.r: MMTC → India's largest international trading organisation and government trading company; Neelachal Ispat Nigam (1982, Kalinga Nagar, Odisha) promoted by MMTC with Odisha government (IPICOL).

05-108.r: Public sector functions: provide public utilities, build social and economic overhead capital, ensure balanced regional and sectoral growth, pursue egalitarian goals.

05-109.r: Public sector in India has basic and heavy industries and secure jobs; not all its industries are profit-oriented.

05-110.r: Public sector employment growth became sluggish because the NEP 1991 reassessed the State's role in development (A and R true; R explains A).

05-111.r: Public sector is most dominant in commercial banking in India (among steel, term-lending institutions and transport).

05-112.r: TISCO (Tata Steel, Jamshedpur, 1907) → private sector; NTPC, SAIL and BHEL → Maharatna CPSEs.

05-113.r: Not a public enterprise → Leather Factory, Gwalior; BHEL Bhopal, Ordnance Factory Jabalpur and Alkaloid Factory Neemuch are public enterprises.

05-114.r: Odd one out → Essar Oil (private; now Nayara Energy); SAIL, BHEL and ONGC are public sector undertakings.

05-115.r: Government holding in BPCL → between 50% and 60% (present 52.98%; it was 66.2% in the question period).
05-115.c: At question time holding was 66.2% (option b); book's answer (c) fits only present data.

05-116.r: Balmer Lawrie (Ministry of Petroleum) and EdCIL (Ministry of Education) → Miniratna-I PSUs; Dredging Corporation (1976) handed to 4 major ports in 2018, so now only 1 and 3.

05-117.r: Private sector refinery now → Essar Oil (Nayara Energy); Bongaigaon, Haldia and Mangalore (MRPL, ONGC subsidiary since March 2003) are public sector.
05-117.c: Book gives no single answer: (c) 2 and 4 fitted the question period, but now only Essar Oil (Nayara Energy) is private; MRPL is an ONGC subsidiary.

05-118.r: Digboi, Barauni, Noonmati and Mathura refineries → all public sector; India has 23 refineries: 19 public, 3 private, 1 joint venture.
05-118.c: No option is correct: all four refineries are in the public sector.

05-119.r: HAL (Bengaluru) → aircraft; founded 23 December 1940 as Hindustan Aircraft Ltd by Walchand Hirachand; management passed to Government of India in 1947.

05-120.r: Electricity generation → NHPC (erstwhile National Hydroelectric Corporation), Miniratna Category-I CPSE and India's largest hydropower organisation.

05-121.r: Tourism and hotel industry development → ITDC (India Tourism Development Corporation, October 1966); Government holds 87.03%.

05-122.r: BSNL → formed in 2000 by corporatisation of the Department of Telecom Services.

05-123.r: 100% Government of India owned enterprise (among BSNL, NTPC, BHEL, SBI) → BSNL.

05-124.r: Loss-making CPSE among ONGC, NTPC, IOC and BSNL → BSNL (in 2013-14 and also in 2022-23).

05-125.r: Top loss-making CPSEs 2014-15: BSNL, Air India, MTNL; in 2022-23 the top loss-maker was HPCL, then BSNL.

05-126.r: GAIL (2009) planned Rs. 8000 crore, 1,100 km gas pipeline from Vijayawada (Andhra Pradesh) to Vijaipur (Madhya Pradesh).

05-127.r: Petrol and diesel prices → decided by oil marketing companies; market-determined from 26 June 2010 (petrol) and 19 October 2014 (diesel).
05-127.t: Petrol was freed first (2010); diesel later (2014).

05-128.r: Navratna → status for selected Central Public Sector Enterprises; first given to 9 CPSEs in 1997; three categories: Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna.

05-129.r: Not Maharatna (February 2013) → Oil India (then Navratna; Maharatna in 2023) and BEL; Maharatna scheme 2010-11; now 13 Maharatna, 20 Navratna, 65 Miniratna.

05-134.r: Maharatna companies → 10 in October 2019; 13 as on 30 April 2024.

05-135.r: Navratna (among Coal India, BHEL, BEL, GAIL) → Bharat Electronics Ltd; other Navratnas include CONCOR, EIL, HAL, MTNL, NALCO, NBCC, NMDC.

05-136.r: MTNL → Navratna; SAIL and GAIL → Maharatna.

05-137.r: Not Navratna → Indian Aluminium Company (private, not a CPSE); SAIL, Power Grid and REC were Navratna then, now Maharatna.
05-137.t: Don't confuse private Indian Aluminium Company with NALCO, the Navratna aluminium CPSE.

05-138.r: NALCO (1981, Bhubaneswar, Ministry of Mines) → Navratna aluminium company; Government holds 51.28% (not BALCO, HINDALCO or MALCO).

05-139.r: Miniratna Category-I → investment autonomy up to Rs. 500 crore or net worth, whichever lower; needs three years' profit, Rs.30 crore pre-tax profit once, positive net worth.

05-140.r: Miniratna (19 September 2006) to six CPSEs: BSNL, BEML, Hindustan Latex, Engineering Projects, Rashtriya Ispat, Garden Reach; Indian Telephone Industries not included.

05-141.r: Rajasthan policies: IT Policy → 2000; Mineral Policy → 2011; Hotel Policy → 2006; Industrial & Investment Promotion Policy → 2010.

05-142.r: Udyami Helpline → call centre of Ministry of MSME; inaugurated 21st August 2010 by Dr. Manmohan Singh; toll-free 1800-180-6763.

05-143.r: Madhya Pradesh Financial Corporation (1955) → headquarters at Indore; finances small and medium industries.
05-143.t: Headquarters is Indore, not the capital Bhopal.

05-144.r: Long-term credit to small and medium enterprises in UP → UP Small Industries Corporation, UPSIDC (now UPSIDA) and UP Financial Corporation: all of these.

05-145.r: UP Financial Corporation (1954, under SFCs Act 1951) → does not finance tourism related industries.

05-146.r: Udyog Bandhu (now Invest UP) → UP government society that facilitates investment and solves establishment and investment problems of industrial units.

05-147.r: Most industrially developed region of Uttar Pradesh → Western UP (more urbanised, more workers in registered factories).

05-148.r: BIFR (Board for Industrial and Financial Reconstruction, Ministry of Finance) → revival or closure of sick industrial units; dissolved 1 December 2016, cases sent to NCLT/NCLAT under IBC.

05-149.r: Mega Food Parks → better infrastructure for food processing; cluster approach linking farmers, processors and retailers to cut wastage and raise farmers' income.

05-151.r: Benefit of industrial development and foreign trade → increased competition (also more goods, higher growth, lower unemployment).

05-152.r: Social objective of business → employment generation (also supply of quality goods); profit earning is an economic objective.

05-153.r: Business process re-engineering with technology: rising customer demands, IT gives competitive edge at lower cost, faster change after liberalisation → all of these.

05-154.r: Sole trader → unlimited liability; Partnership → contractual relationship; Co-operatives → betterment of weaker sections; Public Limited Company → large number of risk bearers.

05-155.r: Acquiring new technology → capital expenditure (buy, upgrade or extend life of assets); debt and equity financing are both capital receipts, not capital vs revenue expenditure.

05-156.r: Venture capital → long-term start-up capital (private equity) for new entrepreneurs and small businesses with growth potential.

05-157.r: First Industrial Policy of free India → April 1948, by Dr. Shyama Prasad Mukherjee (Industry Minister); set a mixed economy model.

05-158.r: Joint Sector concept → Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (second policy, placed by Nehru, April 1956; expand public and co-operative sectors).
05-158.t: 1948 = first policy (mixed economy); 1956 = Industrial Policy Resolution; 1991 = liberalised policy.

05-160.r: Industrial licensing policy drew strength from the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951.

05-161.r: Liberal Industrial Policy adopted → 1991 (amid severe economic instability) to raise efficiency and growth.

05-162.r: Many Indian firms got ISO 9001/9002 certification (BIS) and licensing was liberalised (24 July 1991), but liberalisation does not explain ISO certification.

05-163.r: 1991 Industrial Policy (24 July 1991, P.V. Narasimha Rao) → licence needed only for 18 industries; now only four need compulsory licensing.

05-164.r: Industries needing compulsory licence: 15 at question time (option a); now only four (environmental, safety and strategic reasons).

05-165.r: LPG New Economic Policy (liberalisation, privatisation, globalisation) → announced in 1991 under PM P.V. Narasimha Rao.

05-166.r: Criticisms of Industrial Policy 1991: erratic growth, threat from foreign competition, misplaced faith in foreign investment; neglect of agriculture was not one.

05-167.r: White goods → home appliances (AC, refrigerator, washing machine) bought as conspicuous consumption items; industry delicensed in 1993.

05-168.r: Not correct: 'IPCL is India's largest petrochemicals company' (second in 2002-03; merged with RIL in 2007); MTNL listed on NYSE November 2001.

05-169.r: FMCG = quick-selling, low-cost non-durable goods (toiletries, dairy, bakery); automobiles (car, motorcycle) are not FMCG.

05-170.r: Pearl fishing → Tuticorin; Automobiles → Pune; Shipbuilding → Mormugao; Engineering goods → Pinjore.

05-171.r: Most complete mode of privatisation → transfer of ownership and management to the private sector (divestment).

05-172.r: Disinvestment aims: citizen participation, better governance, lower fiscal burden; Government keeps management control (at least 51%); not mainly to repay external debt.

05-173.r: National Investment Fund (November 2005, disinvestment proceeds) → managed by UTI, SBI and LIC mutual funds; 75% income for social sector schemes, 25% for CPSE capital; a Public Account.
05-173.t: NIF is a Public Account, not part of the Consolidated Fund; it is not managed by the Finance Ministry.

05-174.r: Disinvestment is integral to liberalisation (cuts fiscal burden); proceeds used as per stated policy (NIF, November 2005), but R does not explain A.

05-175.r: Disinvestment is done to cut fiscal burden and revenue shortfall, not because PSUs failed to create jobs (A true, R false).

05-176.r: Disinvestment began in 1991-92: minority stakes in 31 PSUs sold for Rs. 3038 crore.

05-177.r: Steel plant not on a riverside → Bhilai (USSR help, 1959; about 40 km west of Raipur); Bokaro, Jamshedpur, Bhadravati are riverside.

05-178.r: Bhilai Steel Plant (public sector, SAIL) → set up with USSR (Russia) help in Second Five Year Plan; first blast furnace 4th February 1959; about 40 km west of Raipur.

05-180.r: Rourkela Steel Plant → German (West Germany) collaboration; first integrated public sector steel plant; first blast furnace 3rd February 1959; run by SAIL.

05-181.r: Not correct: 'Rourkela set up with Soviet help' (it was German); Salem → stainless steel; Visakhapatnam → RINL; Maharashtra Electrosmelt merged with SAIL in 2011.

05-182.r: Bokaro Steel Plant → Soviet Union (USSR) help; fourth integrated public sector plant; incorporated 29th January 1964, took shape from 1965; later merged with SAIL.

05-183.r: Steel plant collaborations: Rourkela → Germany; Bhilai → USSR; Durgapur → UK; Bokaro → USSR, not USA.
05-183.h: Both 'B' plants (Bhilai, Bokaro) → USSR; D for Durgapur, D for 'Dear old Britain'.

05-184.r: Bhilai → Chhattisgarh; Bokaro → Jharkhand; Durgapur → West Bengal; Rourkela → Odisha.

05-185.r: Jajpur (Odisha) integrated steel plant → Neelachal Ispat Nigam (NINL), not SAIL; Nabinagar (Bihar) → NTPC–Indian Railways joint venture; Jamnagar → Essar Power; Kayamkulam → NTPC.

05-186.r: Indian Diamond Institute (1978) → Surat, Gujarat (diamonds, gems and jewellery).

05-187.r: Cement centres: Katni (Madhya Pradesh), Tirunelveli (Tamil Nadu), Sikka (Gujarat), Churk (Uttar Pradesh).

05-188.r: Visakhapatnam → shipbuilding; Muri (Jharkhand) → aluminium; Gurgaon → automobiles; Panki (UP) → fertilizers.

05-189.r: UP centres: Aonla → fertilizers; Modinagar → rubber; Barabanki → polyfibre; Kanpur → explosives.

05-190.r: Coimbatore → cotton textiles; Rourkela → iron and steel; Kapurthala → rail coach; Barauni → petroleum refining.

05-191.r: Singrauli → coal; Kajarhat (UP) → cement; Koyali (Gujarat) → oil refinery; Anand (Gujarat) → milk.

05-192.r: Tronica City → Ghaziabad, not Noida; Bio-technology Park → Lucknow; Plastic City → Kanpur; Leather Technology Park → Unnao.

05-193.r: National Renewal Fund (February 1992) → safety net for workers hit by modernisation, restructuring or closure of sick units; funded VRS and retraining; not for refugees.

05-198.r: Golden Handshake → Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS), used to cut surplus staff in public and private companies.

05-200.r: POSCO (South Korea, steel) → MoU with Odisha on June 22, 2005 for a 12 billion USD (Rs. 52,000 crore) plant near Paradip.

05-201.r: Kandla (Gulf of Kutch) → Asia's first Export Processing Zone, 1965; now India's largest multi-product SEZ (KASEZ).

05-202.r: Industrial development constrained by: lack of savings to invest, lack of technology, skills and infrastructure, low purchasing power of masses; not lack of entrepreneurship.

05-203.r: Labour intensive industry → employs more hands (labour costs outweigh capital costs), e.g. hotels, agriculture, mining.

05-204.r: Co-partners of industrial relations: workers, managers and Central/State Governments (with their organisations); consumers are not co-partners.

05-205.r: Largest sugar producer → Uttar Pradesh (119.9 lakh tonnes, 2023-24, ISMA), then Maharashtra (99.9) and Karnataka (49.7).

05-206.r: Sugar industry began in UP (first mill Pratappur, Deoria, 1903); low cane yield, short crushing season, poor location caused problems; UP lost lead to Maharashtra in 1960s.

05-207.r: Sugar industry most developed → Uttar Pradesh (leading sugarcane and sugar producing State).

05-208.r: Sugar de-regulation committee → Dr. C. Rangarajan; levy obligation ended for sugar after September 2012, regulated release abolished; 2013-14 a watershed.
05-208.t: Cane area reservation, minimum distance and cane price formula were left to State Governments.

05-209.r: Not matched: Katni – Paper; Katni (MP) is known for cement, limestone and fireclay; Surat → cotton textiles; Churk → cement; Ludhiana → hosiery.

05-211.r: HINDALCO Renukoot (1962) sited for abundant electricity: Renusagar captive power plant (840 MW, 1967), first for aluminium in India.

05-212.r: MALCO → Mettur (Salem, Tamil Nadu), not Chennai; BALCO → Korba; INDAL → Hirakud (now part of HINDALCO); HINDALCO → Renukoot.

05-213.r: Ideal for petrochemicals → Gujarat (infrastructure, strategic location, skilled labour, raw material; leader in chemicals).

05-214.r: Coastal Gujarat → 'industrial workshop' because it is dotted with textile, pharmaceutical and petrochemical units (A and R true; R explains A).

05-215.r: Workers' participation in management → participation of non-managerial employees in policy decision-making.
hi: Workers' participation in management (प्रबंधन में श्रमिक भागीदारी)

05-216.r: Industrial town on the Chota Nagpur plateau ('Ruhr of India') → Ranchi (HEC, mineral based industries).

05-217.r: Dewas (Madhya Pradesh) → Government currency note printing press.

05-218.r: Nature and size of an industry → capital investment, labour force and power consumption (book: turnover also counts today).

05-219.r: First machine-made paper → 1870, Bally near Calcutta; first cement factory → 1904 near Madras; first cotton mill → 1818 Fort Gloster, not 1854 Bombay (second).

05-220.r: First steel attempt Porto Novo (J.M. Heath) 1830; first Bombay textile mill (Davar) 7 July 1854; first jute mill Rishra 1855; first sugar mill Pratappur 1903.
05-220.c: Book's (a) is latest-first by its own dates. Read earliest-first on standard dates (Bombay mill, Rishra jute mill, Tata's first steel, sugar growth around 1930), the order is IV, II, III, I: option (b).

05-221.r: Mundra SEZ → Adani; CMC Ltd → Tata; IPCL → Reliance; VSNL → Tata (Tata Communications, February 2008), not Bharti.

05-222.r: Multinationals in India (book): Samsung and LG; Hindustan Unilever is an Indian subsidiary of Unilever and GKW is not a multinational.

05-223.r: Renault SA → France; Volkswagen AG → Germany; BMW AG → Munich, Germany (not USA); Daimler AG → not Sweden.
05-223.c: The book wrongly places Daimler AG in Coventry, UK; Daimler AG (now Mercedes-Benz Group) is headquartered in Stuttgart, Germany. Answer (b) is still right.

05-224.r: All India Khadi and Village Industries Board → January 1953 (First Plan, 1951-56); KVIC statutory body under KVIC Act 1956, took over in April 1957.

05-225.r: KVIC (statutory commission, Ministry of MSME) → head office at Mumbai.
hi: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (खादी और ग्रामोद्योग आयोग)

05-226.r: Not matched: Tarapore Committee → full capital account convertibility of rupee, not bank customer services; Goswami → industrial sickness; Janakiraman → share scam; Malhotra → insurance reforms.

05-227.r: Meera Seth Committee (12 members, 1995) → handloom development; recommended National Handloom Fund of Rs. 500 crore.

05-228.r: Sathyam Committee (July 1998, report August 1999) → textile policy; basis of National Textile Policy 2000.

05-229.r: National Commission for Enterprises in the Unorganised Sector (NCEUS) → chairman Dr. Arjun Sengupta; set up 20.09.2004; term ended 30.04.2009.

05-230.r: RIICO (Rajasthan; began 28th March 1969 as RSIMDC, split 1st January 1980) → sets up industrial areas, social infrastructure, project reports and managerial services: all these.

05-231.r: RIICO signed MoU with JETRO (Japan External Trade Organization) in July 2008 to bring Japanese units to Neemrana Industrial Area.

05-232.r: State Finance Corporations → mainly finance medium and small scale industries (supplementing Industrial Finance Corporation, IFC Act 1948).

05-233.r: Not matched: Wipro – R. Krishnamurthy; Wipro's founder chairman is Azim Premji (Rishad Premji chairman from 2019); Reliance – Mukesh Ambani; Airtel – Bharti Mittal.

05-234.r: e-Biz portal (Ministry of Commerce and Industry, 28.01.2013) → single window for business access to government services (ease of doing business).
